title: init/update: tag hook entries with `_managedBy: "openwolf"` (fixes #31)
body:
Fixes #31.

## Why

The 6 hook entries OpenWolf installs into `settings.json` carry no
provenance tag. When Claude Code rewrites `settings.json` as part of
an unrelated command — `/effort`, `/config`, plugin toggling, etc. —
entries that don't carry a `_managedBy` field appear to be dropped
silently. The `.wolf/hooks/*.js` files stay on disk, but Claude Code
stops invoking them.

Reproduced on Linux (Claude Code 2.1.121.cc5) and Windows (2.1.126.a4b)
by running `/effort medium` once after `openwolf init`. Confirmed via
file backup that this is a write of `~/.claude/settings.json` from
Claude Code itself (sibling internal-state files mtimed at the same
instant), and that claude-hooks-tagged entries survive the same write.

## What

1. Tag every hook in `HOOK_SETTINGS` (both `init.ts` and `update.ts`)
   with `_managedBy: "openwolf"`. Same field that claude-hooks uses for
   the same purpose.
2. Tighten `replaceOpenWolfHooks` in both files to match by tag OR by
   `.wolf/hooks/` substring. The substring fallback ensures upgrades
   from pre-tag installs clean up correctly.

The TypeScript change is small (32 insertions, 12 deletions across
two files). `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

## Backward compatibility

- Old installs (no tag): substring fallback still picks them up
  for dedupe, so `openwolf update` cleanly removes the old entries
  and installs the tagged versions.
- New installs: tagged from the start, survive Claude Code rewrites.

## Test plan

- [ ] `openwolf init` in a fresh project — verify the 6 entries land
      in `.claude/settings.json` with `_managedBy: "openwolf"`.
- [ ] In Claude Code, run `/effort high`; confirm the openwolf
      entries are still present afterwards (they were dropped before
      this fix).
- [ ] `openwolf update` on a project with the OLD untagged entries —
      verify they get cleanly replaced with the tagged version (no
      duplicates).

title: fix: safe config access with defaults (prevents crash on older .wolf/config.json)
body:
## Summary

Running `openwolf dashboard` (v1.0.4, global install) against an existing `.wolf/config.json` that predates the `dashboard` / `daemon` / `cron` sections crashes immediately:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'port')
    at Command.dashboardCommand (dist/src/cli/dashboard.js:39:44)
      const port = config.openwolf.dashboard.port;
```

`readJSON`'s fallback is whole-file-only — it returns the fallback object **only** when `fs.readFileSync` / `JSON.parse` throws. When the file exists and parses but is missing a nested section (e.g. any config created before that section was added), every accessor along the chain throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. The same class of bug exists in 8 places across the CLI, daemon, and scanner.

## Fix

Replace the 8 unsafe accessors with optional chaining + nullish coalescing to sensible defaults — matching the pattern already used in [src/cli/designqc-cmd.ts:33](https://github.com/cytostack/openwolf/blob/main/src/cli/designqc-cmd.ts#L33) (`config.openwolf?.designqc ?? {}`).

Sites changed:
- `src/cli/dashboard.ts:51` — `dashboard.port`
- `src/cli/daemon-cmd.ts:20` — `dashboard.port`
- `src/cli/cron-cmd.ts:86` — `dashboard.port`
- `src/daemon/wolf-daemon.ts:37` — `daemon.log_level`
- `src/daemon/wolf-daemon.ts:189` — `dashboard.port`
- `src/daemon/wolf-daemon.ts:282` — `cron.enabled`
- `src/daemon/wolf-daemon.ts:291` — `cron.heartbeat_interval_minutes`
- `src/scanner/anatomy-scanner.ts:232-233` — `anatomy.exclude_patterns` + `anatomy.max_files`

Defaults mirror the values already present in each call site's `readJSON(..., fallback)` and the canonical `src/templates/config.json`, so behavior is unchanged for callers whose config has the keys.

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro && git init -q
mkdir -p .wolf && cat > .wolf/config.json <<JSON
{ "version": 1, "openwolf": { "enabled": true, "identity": { "adapter": "claude" } } }
JSON
openwolf dashboard
# → TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'port')
```

With this patch the command proceeds, forks the daemon, and serves the dashboard on 18791.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] Verified manually against v1.0.4 install: daemon binds 18791, `curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:18791` returns HTTP 200
- [x] Reproduction above no longer crashes

## Notes

Root cause discussion: a broader fix would be to deep-merge the fallback inside `readJSON` itself. That changes library semantics for every caller, so this PR sticks to call-site fixes, matching the pattern already chosen in `designqc-cmd.ts`. Happy to rework as a `readJSON` change if maintainers prefer.

title: Feature Request: Git worktree support — hooks, `.wolf/` state, and path resolution
body:
## Summary

OpenWolf's hooks and `.wolf/` state layer assume a single-checkout-per-project model. When a developer works inside a **git worktree** (via `git worktree add` or Claude Code's built-in `--worktree` flag), OpenWolf's hooks either silently fail to fire or crash with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and the `.wolf/` state directory is absent from the worktree entirely. This effectively disables OpenWolf — no anatomy injection, no repeated-read blocking, no token ledger updates, no cerebrum enforcement — without any warning to the developer.

Git worktrees are a common workflow for teams using Claude Code, particularly for parallel feature work, isolated subagent sessions, and CI-driven branch checkouts. This feature request asks for first-class worktree awareness in OpenWolf's init, hook registration, and state management.

## Context

Our team (4–5 developers, Bitbucket monorepo, Gitflow branching) is adopting OpenWolf as a team-wide standard. We committed the shared `.wolf/` knowledge files (`anatomy.md`, `cerebrum.md`, `OPENWOLF.md`, `config.json`, `hooks/`, etc.) and gitignored per-developer state (`memory.md`, `token-ledger.json`, `cron-state.json`, `designqc-captures/`, `backups/`). This works well in the main checkout.

However, several of our developers regularly use git worktrees — both manually created (`git worktree add`) and Claude Code–managed (`claude --worktree` or `claude -w`). In those worktree sessions, OpenWolf is effectively absent.

## Observed behavior

**Scenario A — Developer creates a worktree via `git worktree add ../feature-xyz` and launches Claude Code inside it:**

1. Claude Code looks for `.claude/settings.json` relative to the worktree root. In a linked worktree, `.claude/` may not be present (it lives in the main checkout). If it *is* found (e.g., because it's committed), the hook commands reference `.wolf/hooks/*.js` — but `.wolf/` doesn't exist in the worktree because the per-developer state files are gitignored and the worktree is a fresh checkout.
2. Hooks either silently don't fire (Claude Code doesn't find the settings file at all) or fail with a missing-module error (settings file found, but hook scripts aren't at the expected path).
3. The CLAUDE.md fallback instructions *do* load (since `CLAUDE.md` is tracked), so Claude gets the *instructions* to read `anatomy.md` and `cerebrum.md` — but those files don't exist in the worktree, leading to dead-end references and potential hallucination.

**Scenario B — Developer uses Claude Code's built-in `--worktree` flag:**

Claude Code creates a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. Same outcome as Scenario A: no `.wolf/` directory, hooks don't resolve, state is absent.

**Scenario C — Subagent sessions with worktree isolation:**

Claude Code supports spawning subagent sessions that run in their own worktree for isolation. Each subagent starts a new session inside the worktree. Same outcome: OpenWolf's SessionStart hook doesn't fire (or fires and fails), and the subagent runs without any of OpenWolf's instrumentation. Any learnings from the subagent session are lost when the worktree is cleaned up.

**In all three scenarios, there is no error message, warning, or degraded-mode notification from OpenWolf.** The developer sees a normal-looking Claude Code session and has no way to know OpenWolf isn't running unless they check `openwolf status` or inspect the transcript for missing hook output.

## Upstream Claude Code bugs contributing to this

Several open issues on `anthropics/claude-code` document the hook-resolution problems that affect OpenWolf (and any other hook-based tool) in worktrees:

| Issue | Summary |
|---|---|
| [anthropics/claude-code#46808](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/46808) | Hooks not triggered when working in a git worktree — Claude Code resolves `.claude/settings.json` relative to CWD, not `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` |
| [anthropics/claude-code#36360](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/36360) | `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` expands to the worktree path, so hooks referencing `.claude/helpers/` fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` |
| [anthropics/claude-code#49989](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/49989) | `UserPromptSubmit` hooks silently skip in git worktree sessions |
| [anthropics/claude-code#39277](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/39277) | `PostToolUse:EnterWorktree` hook does not fire when worktree is created via `claude -w` |
| [anthropics/claude-code#42752](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/42752) | `WorktreeCreate` hook can cause `--worktree` flag to hang indefinitely |
| [anthropics/claude-code#27661](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27661) | Subagents do not inherit parent-session hooks or permission rules |

Some of these are Anthropic-side fixes that would help OpenWolf "for free" (especially #46808 — if Claude Code resolved hooks via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the path-resolution problem largely goes away). But others (especially the state-layer question — where does `.wolf/` live when there are multiple worktrees?) require OpenWolf-side design decisions.

## Proposed behavior

Here's what I think worktree-aware OpenWolf could look like. I recognize this is non-trivial and there may be better approaches — these are suggestions, not demands.

### Hook path resolution

`openwolf init` should write hook commands using `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`-prefixed absolute paths rather than bare relative paths (Claude Code's own hooks reference recommends this pattern). For example:

```json
"command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.wolf/hooks/pre-read.js\""
```

This would survive worktree sessions where `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` correctly points to the main repo root (contingent on Anthropic fixing #46808 / #36360, but it's the right thing to do regardless).

### State layer options

The harder question is where `.wolf/` state lives across worktrees. Two possible models:

**Option 1 — Shared state via the main repo (symlink or path resolution):** OpenWolf detects when it's running inside a linked worktree (via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` or checking if `.git` is a file rather than a directory) and resolves `.wolf/` relative to the main repo root rather than CWD. All worktrees read from and write to the same `anatomy.md`, `cerebrum.md`, `buglog.json`, etc. Per-session files (`memory.md`, `token-ledger.json`) could be namespaced by worktree name to avoid write contention.

**Option 2 — Seeded state per worktree:** When OpenWolf's SessionStart hook fires inside a worktree that has no `.wolf/`, it bootstraps a minimal `.wolf/` by copying the committed knowledge files (`anatomy.md`, `cerebrum.md`, `OPENWOLF.md`, `config.json`) from the main repo (located via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` → `..`). The worktree then accumulates its own session-local state. On worktree cleanup, a merge-back step could offer to fold new `cerebrum.md` entries and `buglog.json` entries back into the main checkout's `.wolf/`.

Either option would also need a **detection/warning mechanism**: if the SessionStart hook runs and finds no `.wolf/` and cannot locate one in the main repo, it should log a clear warning (to stderr or the Claude Code transcript) rather than silently doing nothing.

### `openwolf status` in worktrees

`openwolf status` (and `openwolf dashboard`) should report whether the current directory is a linked worktree and, if so, whether it's using shared state from the main repo, seeded local state, or running degraded.

### Documentation

Even before any code changes, documenting the current limitation would be valuable. Something in the README or `docs/troubleshooting.md` like: *"OpenWolf currently requires running in the main checkout of a git repository. Git worktrees (created via `git worktree add` or `claude --worktree`) do not automatically inherit OpenWolf's hooks or `.wolf/` state. If you use worktrees, run `openwolf init` inside each worktree or work from the main checkout."*

## Environment

- OpenWolf v1.0.4 (npm)
- Claude Code (Team plan, CLI)
- Node.js 20
- Git 2.43+ with worktree support
- OS: macOS (primary), Ubuntu 24 (CI)

## Workarounds we're currently using

1. Developers who use worktrees run `openwolf init` inside each new worktree manually. This produces a fresh, empty `.wolf/` that lacks the team's accumulated `cerebrum.md` and `anatomy.md` — the learning memory effectively resets.
2. We committed the shared knowledge files (`anatomy.md`, `cerebrum.md`, `OPENWOLF.md`, `config.json`, `reframe-frameworks.md`, `hooks/`) to the repo so that worktrees inherit them on checkout. Per-developer files remain gitignored. This helps with Scenario A (the files are present), but hooks still don't fire reliably due to the upstream Claude Code issues.
3. For now, we've accepted that worktree sessions run with OpenWolf's CLAUDE.md fallback instructions only — no deterministic hook enforcement, no token ledger, no repeated-read blocking.

Thanks for building OpenWolf — it's been a real improvement for our team's Claude Code workflow in the main checkout, and we're hopeful worktree support can extend that benefit to the rest of our workflow.

title: Multi-project hygiene: init walks up into $HOME, port collisions, and global Claude Code hooks fail in non-openwolf projects
body:
# Multi-project hygiene: init walks up into `$HOME`, port collisions, and global Claude Code hooks fail in non-openwolf projects

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 26.3 (Tahoe 26.3.0, build 25D125)
- **Node.js:** v25.9.0
- **OpenWolf:** v1.0.4
- **Claude Code:** 2.1.114
- **pm2:** installed via npm (default config)

## Summary

`openwolf init` across multiple projects on the same machine cascades through several design gaps. None are individually fatal, but together they left me with a crash-looping daemon, a stale install at `$HOME`, and every Claude Code session in an unrelated project throwing `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on the Stop hook.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Clean slate
rm -rf ~/.wolf
pm2 delete all

# Project A — works as expected
cd ~/dev/project-a && openwolf init
# ✓ creates ~/dev/project-a/.wolf/, pm2 entry online

# Run init without cd'ing into a project dir first
cd ~ && openwolf init
# ✓ creates ~/.wolf/, pm2 adds a daemon for $HOME
# That daemon silently crash-loops on port 18790 (already taken by project-a)

# Try to recover by initializing a different project
cd ~/dev/project-b && openwolf init
# CLI prints: "Project root: $HOME"
# Walks up, finds ~/.wolf/, "upgrades" that one instead of creating ./.wolf/

# In any Claude Code session in a dir without .wolf/, every Stop/Read/Write
# tool call now prints:
#   Error: Cannot find module '$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.wolf/hooks/stop.js'
```

## Expected vs actual

| # | Expected | Actual |
|---|----------|--------|
| 1 | `openwolf init` in a child dir initializes there | Walks up through ancestors, stops at first `.wolf/` found — in my case `~/.wolf`, making every subsequent init silently "upgrade" the `$HOME` install |
| 2 | Init at `$HOME` prompts or refuses | Silent success. Spawns a daemon, scans the home dir for anatomy (capped to 500 files but no warning) |
| 3 | Daemon picks a free port | Every `config.json` hardcodes daemon `18790`, dashboard `18791`. Second daemon fails with `EADDRINUSE` |
| 4 | Failed daemon bind surfaces loudly | Init prints `✓ Daemon: running via pm2` even when the daemon is crash-looping. Have to run `pm2 list` / `pm2 logs` manually to notice |
| 5 | Global Claude Code hooks no-op in projects without `.wolf/` | Hooks are registered in `~/.claude/settings.json` as unconditional `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.wolf/hooks/stop.js"`. They fire in every project and throw `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` when `.wolf/` isn't present |
| 6 | `pm2` entries are uniquely named | Name is `openwolf-<basename(cwd)>`. Two projects with the same basename would collide silently |
| 7 | A diagnostic command exists to catch all of the above | No `openwolf doctor` / `openwolf status --all`. Had to piece together pm2 state, config ports, and hook paths by hand |

## Relevant logs

pm2 state after the home-dir init (names redacted):

```
┌────┬────────────────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬──────┐
│ id │ name               │ status │ uptime  │ mem    │ ↺    │
├────┼────────────────────┼────────┼─────────┼────────┼──────┤
│ 0  │ openwolf-<project> │ online │ 5D      │ 92.1mb │ 0    │
```

```
Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::18791
  at Server.setupListenHandle [as _listen2] (node:net:2008:16)
```

Claude Code stop-hook failure in a project without `.wolf/`:

```
Ran 3 stop hooks

Error: Cannot find module '<project>/.wolf/hooks/stop.js'
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

## Suggestions

1. **Anchor root detection on a project marker, not on `.wolf/`.** Use `.git`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, or an explicit `.openwolf-root` file. Fall back to cwd. Never climb past `$HOME`. At minimum, refuse to initialize when the resolved root is `$HOME` without `--force-home`.
2. **Auto-allocate ports on init.** Probe a free pair and write them into `config.json`. Or use a UNIX domain socket for IPC and only bind TCP for the dashboard on demand.
3. **Fail init loudly when the daemon can't bind.** Check daemon health for a few seconds after pm2 start; print the port conflict instead of `✓ Daemon: running via pm2`.
4. **Guard Claude Code hooks or register them per-project.** Either wrap each command with `test -f "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.wolf/hooks/stop.js" && node ...`, or write hooks into `$PROJECT/.claude/settings.json` during `openwolf init` so they only fire where a `.wolf/` exists.
5. **Disambiguate pm2 names** — include a path hash (`openwolf-<base>-3f2a`) or parent segment.
6. **Ship `openwolf doctor`.** One command that lists registered projects, daemon status, port collisions, orphaned pm2 entries, and hook resolution.

## Workaround

```
pm2 delete openwolf-<home> && pm2 save
mv ~/.wolf ~/.wolf-home-backup
cd <real project> && openwolf init
# edit .wolf/config.json to bump daemon/dashboard off 18790/18791
pm2 restart openwolf-<project> && pm2 save
```

Happy to open a PR for (1), (4), and (6) if there's interest.

title: Invalid signature in thinking
body:
````markdown
## Bug: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block on multi-turn conversations with extended thinking enabled

**Severity:** High — breaks all multi-turn conversations when extended thinking is active  
**Component:** Conversation history / message assembly  
**API:** Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`)

---

### Description

When extended thinking is enabled, multi-turn conversations fail with a 400 error on the second request:

````
API Error: 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",
"message":"messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block"}}
````

### Root Cause

The Anthropic API requires that `thinking` blocks in assistant messages are passed back **verbatim** in subsequent requests. Each `thinking` block contains a `signature` field that the API uses to verify the content has not been tampered with between turns.

OpenWolf appears to be mangling the assistant message content when building conversation history — likely by:

- Deserialising/reserialising message content and dropping the `signature` field
- Extracting only `type: "text"` blocks and discarding `thinking` blocks
- Reconstructing or summarising assistant content rather than storing/replaying it as-is

The result is a `thinking` block with a missing or empty `signature` being sent back to the API:

```json
{
  "type": "thinking",
  "thinking": "...",
  "signature": ""
}
```

### Expected Behaviour

Assistant message content arrays (including `thinking` blocks) must be stored and replayed exactly as received from the API. The `signature` field is non-negotiable — it cannot be omitted, emptied, or regenerated.

Per Anthropic's documentation, there are only two valid approaches for handling `thinking` blocks in conversation history:

1. **Pass them back whole** — store the entire content block including `type`, `thinking`, and `signature`, and include it verbatim in subsequent turns.
2. **Omit them entirely** — the API permits dropping `thinking` blocks from prior turns in the history. What it does not permit is including them with an invalid or missing `signature`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable extended thinking in settings
2. Start a new conversation and send any message
3. Send a follow-up message in the same conversation

**Result:** 400 error on the second request  
**Expected:** Successful response

### Suggested Fix

In the message history assembly layer, ensure assistant messages are stored as the complete raw content array returned by the API — not reconstructed or filtered. When replaying history, either include `thinking` blocks exactly as stored, or strip them entirely before sending. Do not include them in a partially reconstructed state.

### Environment

- OpenWolf version: 1.0.4
- Extended thinking: enabled
- Model: Sonnet 4.6
````

```bash
openwolf init --opencode
```

title: Fix dashboard bugs: Run Now, AI Insights, token chart, Design QC, project switching, cron logging
body:
This PR fixes 8 bugs found during real usage of the OpenWolf dashboard. No new features — all fixes.

## Bug 1 — "Run Now" button silently did nothing

The button called `client?.send()` over WebSocket which drops silently if the socket is not in OPEN state. Replaced with `fetch POST /api/cron/run/:taskId`. The endpoint returns 202 immediately and runs the task in the background. If the task fails, a `task_error` WebSocket message is broadcast so the UI shows the actual error instead of resetting silently.

## Bug 2 — AI Insights "Generate Now" opened the Claude desktop app

The cron engine was spawning the `claude` CLI binary from a background daemon. On macOS that binary spins up a Linux VM via the Virtualization framework and delegates auth to the desktop app — both fail from a headless process. Fix: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, call the Anthropic API directly via `fetch`. If not set, fail immediately with a clear error. The dashboard panel now shows a copy-able prompt to paste into a Claude Code session — how OpenWolf is meant to work (Claude writes data, the dashboard reads it).

## Bug 3 — Token graph x-axis showed date only, not time

`s.started.slice(0, 10)` only kept the date. Changed to `.slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ")` to show `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`.

## Bug 4 — Design QC only worked on localhost

The capture engine only detected dev servers. Added `detectDeployedUrl()` which checks `package.json` homepage, `.env.production` URL vars, and `vercel.json` aliases. Added a manual "Run Capture" button with `POST /api/designqc/run` endpoint. Fixed the engine not writing `designqc-report.json` after capture.

## Bug 5 — Token comparison chart had hardcoded data and visual issues

Removed fabricated comparison data. Now uses real tracked values from the token ledger. Fixed the gray tail on bars (recharts renders a background behind each bar by default — set `background` fill to transparent). Fixed tooltip using undefined CSS variables — now uses explicit dark colors. Labels updated to be honest: "With OpenWolf (actual)" vs "Without OpenWolf (est.)".

## Bug 6 — "Healthy" and "Live" badges were meaningless

The sidebar badge always showed green regardless of actual state. The header Live indicator added noise without value — if the page loaded, the daemon is running. Both removed.

## Bug 7 — Dashboard showed wrong project after switching

All projects default to port 18791. Starting a second project's daemon failed silently because the port was already held, leaving the old project's dashboard visible. `daemonStart` now kills whatever is on the port before starting. Added `POST /api/switch` which hot-reloads the project in-place: stops the cron engine and file watcher, swaps the project root, restarts both subsystems, broadcasts the new project's full state over the existing WebSocket. No process restart needed. Added a project switcher dropdown in the dashboard header.

## Bug 8 — Cron execution log was never written

The daemon writes `cron-state.json` on startup with only `{ engine_status, last_heartbeat }`. When tasks completed and tried to append to `execution_log`, they hit `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` — caught by the task's own catch block, making every successful run look like a failure. Fixed by merging stored state with complete defaults in `readState()` so `execution_log` is always an array.

## Also: openwolf binary lost execute bit on every build

`tsc` does not preserve the `+x` bit. Added `chmod +x` to the `build` script and a `postinstall` hook so it is set automatically after every build and `npm install -g`.
